why_lead: Peloton was the largest one-session equity mover on the card (37.27 USD, +25.28% on 2022-02-08; +33.01% over five sessions; now +8.44% over 20) and the 8 February catalyst is new and concrete: Foley stepping down with about 2,800 job cuts [[n0827]], [[n0828]], new CEO Barry McCarthy [[n0813]], [[n0826]], activist Blackwells pushing for more [[n0758]], plus mainstream attention (NYT 'What Is Peloton Worth?' [[n1192]], Wirecutter [[n1173]], Marketing Brew [[n1194]]). Relation to earlier retail notes: Peloton appeared only as a secondary item on 2022-02-07 (takeover lottery ticket, WSJ report) and 2022-02-08 (the +20.93% takeover pop); this promotion to lead is justified by newly published 8 February evidence of a different catalyst (management reset and cost cuts) rather than the takeover rumour, which is now only background. The 2022-02-01 and 2022-02-02 drafts did not cover Peloton.
why_smaller: AMC Entertainment: the meme-revival reflex with a new company catalyst — AMC +10.19% and GameStop +12.96% on 8 February, AMC's URW lease agreements and ArcLight acquisitions [[n0754]], [[n0753]], MarketWatch's meme-era tax-bill tally [[n0735]]. Relation to earlier notes: the 2022-02-01 lead was GameStop ('one year on, the faithful buy again'); this is a secondary item with a new AMC-specific catalyst, not a repeat of that lead.

Bitcoin: a different crypto narrative from the 2022-02-08 'crypto spring' lead — the Justice Department's $3.6 billion seizure [[n0807]] and the laundering charges [[n0955]] (8 February, known per timing), TMX crypto futures [[n0944]], scams [[n1797]]; card BTC 44,118.45 USD, +18.74% over five days but +5.69% over 20, DOGE -4.33%. Kept secondary because the price story is unchanged and only the catalyst is new.

Nvidia: the leveraged-chip narrative after the confirmed Arm termination ([[n0823]], [[n1950]], [[n0843]], [[n0788]]), NVDA +1.54%, MRVL +6.89%, SOXL +7.35% but -22.33% over 20 sessions versus SOXX -6.30%; inflation-data focus [[n1348]] as the trigger. Not covered in any earlier retail note.
